title: The text discusses Shell's ongoing campaign to replace and bury flowlines in Nigeria, which has faced delays due to budget cutbacks. While only 210 kilometers of flowlines were replaced against a target of 955 kilometers, Shell plans to prioritize areas near populated regions. The company also faced challenges from sabotage, which significantly increased the volume of oil spills, despite a decrease in the number of incidents. Shell's efforts to improve community welfare in the Niger Delta included healthcare initiatives, vocational training, and educational support. Additionally, the text touches on a gas project in Mozambique, highlighting its potential for job creation and the complexities surrounding Mozambique's debt relief under the HIPC initiative.
